description:
FILED s481b (2026-09-10, Opus) from the group-B probes of the
critical-infrastructure measurement (#1607).  Socket / IO::Socket is on the
README's infrastructure list, so #1574 will be picked up, and as written its
DIAGNOSIS sends the reader to a file that is already correct.

#1574 says: "lib/Socket.pm does not export AF_UNIX, so loading IO::Socket::UNIX
dies 'Undefined subroutine &IO::Socket::UNIX::AF_UNIX' â one shim edit".

THE SYMPTOM IS REAL AND IT MATTERS MORE THAN #1574 CLAIMED â it is what stops
HTTP::Tiny once that dist compiles at all (s481b's `while ()` fix), so it is on
the critical path for a listed infrastructure module:

    require IO::Socket;                     # perl: loaded
                                            # PCL : Undefined subroutine
                                            #       &IO::Socket::UNIX::AF_UNIX

BUT THE DIAGNOSIS IS WRONG, measured (scratch/s481b/probe-socket-import.pl,
probe-iosocket.pl, probe-iosocket2.pl, probe-second-import.pl,
probe-exporter-export.pl), perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl:

  * `lib/Socket.pm` line 20 ALREADY lists `AF_UNIX` in `@EXPORT` (with
    `@EXPORT_OK = @EXPORT`) and line 40 defines it as `use constant AF_UNIX => 1`.
  * Both import spellings work under PCL and agree with perl â
    `use Socket qw(AF_UNIX SOCK_STREAM)` and a plain `use Socket` â and so does
    a SECOND importer package importing a different subset after a first.
  * **`require IO::Socket::UNIX` on its own LOADS under PCL** â the exact thing
    #1574 says dies.
  * `Exporter::export('Socket', $callpkg, @list)` â the call `IO::Socket::import`
    makes, which is how `IO::Socket::UNIX` gets `AF_UNIX` â also works when
    written by hand.
  * A sub DEFINED LATER in a file is callable from a statement earlier in it
    (perl's whole-file compile), so IO::Socket's `require IO::Socket::UNIX` at
    line 22 seeing `sub import` at line 32 is NOT the difference either.

So the failure needs the real `IO/Socket.pm` load path â the circular
`IO::Socket` â `require IO::Socket::UNIX` â `use IO::Socket` â `IO::Socket::import`
â `Exporter::export 'Socket'` â and none of its pieces reproduces alone.
Whoever takes it should instrument that chain rather than edit an export list.

ALSO MEASURED, and a DIFFERENT bug in the same neighbourhood:
`require IO::Socket::INET` (alone, no `IO::Socket`) dies with

    Value of pcl::h in (sb-impl::gethash3 k h nil)
    is #S(p-typeglob :package #<package "Symbol"> :name "gen0"), not a HASH-TABLE.

which is `Symbol::gensym`'s `delete $$genpkg{$name}` â a symbolic deref of the
STASH `%Symbol::`, i.e. `docs/not-supported.md` "Live symbol-table hashes
(%main::, %Foo::)  [DEFERRED]".  Two failures, two causes; #1614's glob-as-hash
is a third, adjacent one.  Do not assume one fix covers them.

A METHOD NOTE WORTH KEEPING (it is how s481b first mis-read this): the very
first probe ran `require IO::Socket::INET` in a loop AFTER several XS modules
had already failed, and the error text then named `IO::Socket::UNIX::AF_UNIX`.
Probed alone, each module gives a different answer.  **A load-order-dependent
error message is not a diagnosis.**

ACTION: keep #1574 open, replace its cause line with "reproduces through
`require IO::Socket`, not through `IO::Socket::UNIX`; the export list is
correct", and re-measure the Data-Dump `t/glob.t` row it was filed for against
both spellings.
subject: CORRECTION to #1574 (keep it open, fix its cause line): the symptom is real and blocks HTTP::Tiny â `require IO::Socket` dies "Undefined subroutine &IO::Socket::UNIX::AF_UNIX" â but `lib/Socket.pm` DOES export AF_UNIX and `require IO::Socket::UNIX` alone LOADS, so the export list is not the bug; it needs the circular IO::Socket load path.  Separately, `require IO::Socket::INET` dies on a LIVE STASH in Symbol::gensym.
